classes.name: Templar
classes.tagline: AION 2's only dedicated tank — the immovable front line every serious group builds around.
classes.overview: Templar is the game's sole main tank, converting shield skills into threat and party-wide mitigation — and shield skills conditionally unlock its hardest-hitting skill, Judgment. Group-utility tier lists rank it S-tier across PvE, raids and Abyss PvP for exactly that reason.
classes.playstyle: Hold aggro with a tight provoke loop, face bosses away from the party (most cleaves are frontal), and rotate defensive cooldowns against scripted burst windows. In PvP Templars anchor pushes and peel for carries.
strengths: Only dedicated tank at launch — permanent raid demand
S-tier in group-utility PvE and PvP rankings
Shield skills unlock Judgment: real tank damage spikes
Forgiving entry with a high cooldown-management ceiling
weaknesses: Low solo farming speed
Damage depends entirely on group uptime
Mistimed defensive cooldowns can wipe a raid attempt

skillChains.name: Judgment Unlocked
skillChains.description: The signature Templar loop — landing shield skills conditionally unlocks Judgment, your biggest hit and threat spike.
steps: Open with Vicious Strike to build initial threat
Follow with Shield Smite — landing shield skills lights up Judgment
Fire Judgment the moment it unlocks
Repeat the loop; never let Judgment sit unlocked while the cooldown idles
tips: Stack the hotbar slot: Vicious Strike below Judgment so the auto-fallback keeps the loop smooth
Keep long-cooldown defensives manual — official macro guidance says never macro movement or defensive skills

skillChains.name: Aggro & Bulwark
skillChains.description: Threat discipline and mitigation timing — the unglamorous half of tanking that decides raid attempts.
steps: Provoke on cooldown — most raid wipes start with a lost taunt
Face the boss away from the party (frontal cleaves are standard)
Rotate personal mitigation against scripted burst windows
Coordinate big defensive skills with your Cleric's heals
tips: Call your mitigation in chat so healers can spend mana elsewhere
Sanctuary raids allow only 2 revives per encounter — your positioning is a resource

macros.name: Threat Loop
macros.useCase: Official Skill Macro slot (K → Skill Macro; bottom slot = highest priority). Hold the key to cycle — set delay 10–20 ms on low ping, 40–50 ms above ~80 ms, and turn the separate Skill Queue option OFF.

macros.name: Panic Save
macros.useCase: Emergency personal defense stack. Keep it on a separate manual key rather than macroing it into your damage loop.

priority: Craft the gold Chalice first and lock your core threat/rotation skill
Frontal damage amplification — you fight face-to-face all fight
Weapon Damage Amplification > Crit/General Amp > Max Attack
Only enhance gold cards whose 4 skill lines are 3–4 Templar skills; bank materials otherwise
arcana.notes: Arcana is a card system (Chalice, Parchment, Bell, Mirror, Scales, Key, Hourglass, Dice, Lantern) with mixable 2-piece/4-piece set bonuses. Each gold-card enhancement upgrades one of its 4 skill lines at random — no pity — so cards with wrong lines are set-bonus fodder, not enhance targets.

priority: Clear the 4 skill boards first (Nezekan → Zikel → Vaizel → Triniel) for +4 total skill levels
Skill-level nodes before anything else — they multiply every other investment
Then attack nodes, then survivability; skip MP/crit-resist nodes
PvE: points into the Ariel stat board; PvP: Azphel
daevanion.notes: Daevanion in AION 2 is a node-board system, not wearable gear. Boards unlock at level thresholds (Nezekan ~13, Zikel 20, Vaizel 30, Triniel 40); nodes cost 1/2/3/4 points (gray/green/blue/orange). The late-game Marchutan/Yustiel boards were reported absent from Global at launch.

gearProgression.notes: Don't invest — roll substats on cheap gold gear to transfer later.

gearProgression.focus: Vakron armor (+ Aulamus accessories from Urugugu)
gearProgression.notes: The first tier worth enhancing and transferring into — see the Gear Transfer guide.
Block/HP rolls matter more than threat here — DPS carries damage checks.

gearProgression.focus: Ludra raid set + crafted Splendent pieces
gearProgression.notes: Enhance to +15 (last 5 steps can fail — item is safe, +5% pity per fail).

classes.name: Gladiator
classes.tagline: The greatsword bruiser — sustained cleave, self-sustain and an S-tier Abyss PvP rating.
classes.overview: Gladiator trades the shield for raw two-handed damage: documented community sequences run Rage Burst → Overhead Slam → Rending Blow, and game8 ranks it S-tier for raw PvE output. It also off-tanks when your Templar is busy.
classes.playstyle: Ramp through the Rage Burst loop, weave sustain to shrug off chip damage, and stay glued to the boss's back for rear-positioning damage. In PvP Gladiators punish isolated targets and rank S-tier in Abyss ratings.
strengths: S-tier raw damage (game8) and S-tier Abyss PvP rating
Easy-to-medium difficulty — the best melee entry point
Self-sustain reduces healer burden
Off-tank utility when the Templar needs help
weaknesses: Melee range in a telegraph-heavy game
PvP burst is predictable against organized teams
Group-utility lists rank it below the S-tier supports

skillChains.name: Rage Burst Loop
skillChains.description: The documented community damage sequence — rage generation into the heavy Overhead Slam, cashed with Rending Blow.
steps: Build rage with your basic builders
Pop Rage Burst when the damage window opens
Land Overhead Slam inside the buff window
Finish with Rending Blow before the window closes
tips: Stack this sequence into one Skill Macro slot (bottom = highest priority) and hold the key
Frontal amplification Arcana fits Gladiator — you're face-to-face with the boss all fight

skillChains.name: Sustain & Offtank
skillChains.description: The bruiser half — self-healing weaves and emergency aggro when things go sideways.
steps: Weave your sustain skill after the boss's AoE patterns, not after you're already low
Hold off-tank aggro on adds when the Templar is committed to the boss
Drop your defensive skill before telegraphed heavies
Re-anchor to the boss's rear for the damage window
tips: Gladiators make raid adds-phase offtanks — practice the aggro grab on trash
Sanctuary attempts are consumed on entry: stay alive, even at damage cost

macros.name: Rage Burst Sequence
macros.useCase: Documented community sequence as one official Skill Macro slot — hold the key to cycle, delay 10–20 ms on low ping (40–50 ms high ping), Skill Queue OFF.

macros.name: Sustain Weave
macros.useCase: Keeps healing woven into the rotation without a dedicated press.

priority: Craft the gold Chalice first and lock Overhead Slam (the documented community example)
Frontal damage amplification — melee face-time is guaranteed
Weapon Damage Amplification > Crit/General Amp > Max Attack
Only enhance gold cards with 3–4 Gladiator skill lines; bank the rest
arcana.notes: The crafted Chalice can lock one chosen skill (community testing rolled ~1-in-18 odds without it), which is why 'gold grail first' is the standard Arcana route. Transmutation: 5 Mysterious Crystals + 2,000,000 Kinah guarantees one skill.

priority: Clear all 4 skill boards first (+4 total skill levels — includes your core rotation)
Attack nodes next, survivability last; skip MP/crit-resist nodes
PvE focus: Ariel board; PvP focus: Azphel board
Watch for the known PvP-useless nodes: Multi-hit Resist (Triniel), Crit Damage Tolerance (Vaizel)
daevanion.notes: Node costs: gray 1, green (passive) 2, blue (active) 3, orange (percent) 4. Points come from side quests, Sealed Dungeons and the one-time Shugo Festival purchase (50 pts); crystals are tradeable on the Auction House.

gearProgression.notes: The weapon is the only slot that matters — save everything else.
Your first real investment target — enhance and transfer here.
Crafted gear gives ~+5% PvE over same-tier dungeon gear — worth it for weapons.
+10→+15 rates run 65/50/35/25/20% with +5% pity; budget Kinah accordingly (~15M average from +0).

classes.name: Assassin
classes.tagline: The hardest class in the game — dual-dagger burst that deletes targets, and the Abyss's most feared ganker.
classes.overview: Assassin tops the difficulty curve (game8's hardest ease-of-use rating; ping-sensitive above ~100 ms) and pays you back with S-tier PvP ratings from game8 and BlueStacks. Its kit is crit-gated: Heart Gore only opens after critical hits.
classes.playstyle: Track crits to unlock Heart Gore, cycle Insignia Explosion → Heart Gore → Savage Roar, and exit before retaliation. In the Abyss, Assassins define the ganking meta — but only with clean execution.
strengths: S-tier PvP rating (game8, BlueStacks)
Highest skill ceiling in the game
Crit-gated Heart Gore rewards mastery with huge spikes
Rear-position amplification fits its playstyle perfectly
weaknesses: Hardest rotation to execute — ping-sensitive (~100 ms+ hurts)
Group-utility tier lists rank it B for PvE
Squishy once burst cooldowns are spent

skillChains.name: Heart Gore Window
skillChains.description: The documented Assassin sequence — crits unlock Heart Gore, and the whole rotation is built around cashing it.
steps: Open with Insignia Explosion
Land criticals to unlock Heart Gore
Fire Heart Gore the instant it lights up
Reset the cycle with Savage Roar
tips: Stack the sequence into one Skill Macro slot — hold the key, bottom slot highest priority
Rear amplification Arcana is the Assassin pick — you live behind the boss

skillChains.name: Positioning Discipline
skillChains.description: Survival through never being where the damage is — the skill that separates good Assassins from floor-lore.
steps: Pre-position behind the boss before mechanic windows
Save your escape skill for telegraphs, not for greed
Peel resets between burst windows instead of face-tanking
Re-enter through flanks — never through the frontal cone
tips: Sanctuary raids allow 2 revives per encounter — dead Assassins deal zero damage
If your ping is above ~100 ms, tighten your delay settings to 40–50 ms in the macro editor

macros.name: Burst Sequence
macros.useCase: Documented community sequence as one official Skill Macro slot. Delay matters more for Assassins than any class — 10–20 ms low ping, 40–50 ms high ping, Skill Queue OFF.

macros.name: Escape Hatch
macros.useCase: Official guidance: keep movement and defensive skills manual — that's exactly what this key is for.

priority: Craft the gold Chalice first and lock Heart Gore
Rear damage amplification — the Assassin-specific pick
Weapon Damage Amplification > Crit/General Amp > Max Attack
Only enhance gold cards whose lines are 3–4 Assassin skills
arcana.notes: Arcana skill lines are the quiet Assassin multiplier: each gold-card enhancement upgrades one of 4 lines at random, so a card with Heart Gore + crit skills is worth more than any stat card.

priority: Clear the 4 skill boards first (+4 total skill levels — prioritize Heart Gore nodes)
Attack nodes next; skip MP/crit-resist nodes entirely
PvE: Ariel board; PvP: Azphel board (Assassins usually run both)
Avoid the known PvP-useless nodes: Multi-hit Resist (Triniel), Crit Damage Tolerance (Vaizel)
daevanion.notes: Skill boards unlock at ~13/20/30/40 (Nezekan, Zikel, Vaizel, Triniel) and share one currency; stat boards (Ariel/Azphel) each use their own. PvP currency: Monolith feathers, weekly 10v10 Battlefields, Abyss Points shop.

gearProgression.notes: Execution matters more than gear until ~1,400 GS.
Dual-wield = two transfer targets — budget accordingly.
Rear-amp positioning starts paying off visibly at this tier.
KR logs reportedly favor Assassin/Ranger in late-game parsing — the ceiling is real.

classes.name: Ranger
classes.tagline: The easy-to-play ranged powerhouse — sustained bow damage, traps, and uptime that never drops.
classes.overview: Ranger is the best low-difficulty DPS in the game: game8 ranks it S-tier for raw PvE damage with an easy-to-medium difficulty rating. The documented sequence Gale Arrow → Marking Shot → Snare Shot carries most fights.
classes.playstyle: Keep the bow cycling through the Gale Arrow sequence, use traps to control space, and never stop attacking — instant skills keep uptime during movement phases. In PvP Rangers kite melee and rank A-tier in the Abyss.
strengths: S-tier raw PvE damage (game8) at easy-to-medium difficulty
Ranged uptime through mechanics that displace melee
Traps and mobility control fights
Strong A-tier Abyss PvP presence
weaknesses: Group-utility lists (Mobalytics) rank it B for PvE
Damage drops when forced into full movement
Squishy when a melee closes the gap

skillChains.name: Marked Volley
skillChains.description: The documented Ranger sequence — marks the target, snares it, and keeps arrows flying through the whole window.
steps: Open with Gale Arrow for the burst tick
Apply Marking Shot to the priority target
Root with Snare Shot when adds or players push in
Reset the cycle with your basic attack skill
tips: Stack the sequence into one Skill Macro slot — hold the key to cycle, Skill Queue OFF
Pre-trap choke points before pulls instead of reacting late

skillChains.name: Deadshot Discipline
skillChains.description: Uptime and positioning — the ranged-damage habits that make Ranger's numbers look effortless.
steps: Fire Deadshot inside the damage window, from max range
Never cast during the boss's dash — instant skills keep uptime
Save the escape skill for telegraphs you can't sidestep
Re-anchor to max range after every reposition
tips: Ranger damage is uptime-driven — movement discipline beats raw stats
Kite melee in the Abyss around guards; enemy outpost guards one-shot under-geared players

macros.name: Volley Sequence
macros.useCase: Documented community sequence as one official Skill Macro slot — hold the key, delay 10–20 ms low ping / 40–50 ms high ping, Skill Queue OFF.

macros.name: Kite Escape
macros.useCase: Roots the pursuer and buys distance. Manual key — official guidance says keep movement skills out of damage macros.

priority: Craft the gold Chalice first and lock your core rotation skill
Weapon Damage Amplification > Crit/General Amp > Max Attack
Directional amps matter less — reposition freely without losing value
Only enhance gold cards with 3–4 Ranger skill lines
arcana.notes: Ranger is one of the few classes where positional amplification (front/rear) is skippable — uptime from max range is the actual multiplier.

priority: Clear the 4 skill boards first (+4 total skill levels)
Attack nodes next; skip MP/crit-resist nodes
PvE: Ariel board; PvP: Azphel board
Skip the known PvP-useless nodes (Multi-hit Resist on Triniel, Crit Damage Tolerance on Vaizel)
daevanion.notes: Daevanion crystals are tradeable on the Auction House — Rangers with spare Kinah can shortcut the stat boards.

gearProgression.notes: The bow is ~60% of your damage — prioritize it above armor.
First real investment target — enhance and transfer here.
Game8's S-tier raw damage assumes a kept-up weapon — don't fall behind here.
KR parsing reportedly favors Ranger in late-game — the ceiling holds at ilvl 102.

classes.name: Sorcerer
classes.tagline: The magic burst cannon — Hellfire nukes, cast-time discipline, and A-tier ratings everywhere.
classes.overview: Sorcerer is the ranged magic burst benchmark: S-tier raw damage on game8, A-tier on Mobalytics PvE and PvP. It's rated medium-hard to play — cast times punish sloppy positioning harder than any other ranged class.
classes.playstyle: Pre-position before big casts, unload Hellfire and burst inside damage windows, and cancel casts into movement the moment mechanics demand it. In PvP Sorcerers are lethal behind a screen and feed kills when caught.
strengths: S-tier raw PvE damage (game8)
A-tier PvE and PvP on Mobalytics' group-utility scale
Huge burst windows for burn checks
Ranged magic damage — positional amps barely matter
weaknesses: Medium-hard difficulty rating
Cast times punished by movement-heavy fights
Glass build — caught Sorcerers die fast

skillChains.name: Hellfire Burn
skillChains.description: The standard burn loop — set up, amplify, then unload the nuke inside the damage window.
steps: Pre-position before the window opens
Apply your amplification/setup skill
Cast Hellfire inside the window
Cancel into movement the instant mechanics demand it
tips: Start the cast so it lands as the window opens — late Sorcerers lose whole windows
Boss dashes end casts: cancel early, re-anchor, resume

skillChains.name: Blink Discipline
skillChains.description: Survival through positioning — the habits that keep a glass cannon alive in A-tier content.
steps: Save the escape/blink skill for telegraphs, not for greed
Stand with the ranged group, not mid-arena
Use CC utility on rampaging adds
Re-anchor to max range after every reposition
tips: Never finish a cast into a telegraph — the death recap always shows it
Sanctuary raids allow 2 revives: dead glass cannons deal zero damage

macros.name: Burn Window
macros.useCase: Aligns setup and nuke in one held key. Longest-cooldown skill first (official guidance); delay 10–20 ms low ping, 40–50 ms high ping, Skill Queue OFF.

macros.name: Glass Escape
macros.useCase: Panic combo for divers. Manual key — movement and defensives stay out of damage macros per official guidance.

priority: Craft the gold Chalice first and lock Hellfire
Weapon Damage Amplification > Crit/General Amp > Max Attack
Magic scaling makes flat attack less valuable than amplification
Only enhance gold cards with 3–4 Sorcerer skill lines
arcana.notes: Arcana card sets (Primal Vigor for PvE offense, Guardian for defense) mix at 2-piece/4-piece — Sorcerers typically run offense sets and solve survivability with positioning.

priority: Clear the 4 skill boards first (+4 total skill levels — Hellfire nodes first)
Attack nodes next; skip MP/crit-resist nodes
PvE: Ariel board; PvP: Azphel board
Skip known PvP-useless nodes (Multi-hit Resist, Crit Damage Tolerance)
daevanion.notes: Points come from side quests, Sealed Dungeons and the Shugo Festival one-time purchase (50 pts). Weekly Ascension Trial fragments feed the PvE stat-board currency.

gearProgression.notes: Mana problems disappear with decent gear — don't overinvest early.
First transfer target — weapon first, always.
Burn-window damage starts one-shotting trash packs at this tier.
Hold burst cooldowns for raid burn windows — desynced Sorcerers waste the check.

classes.name: Spiritmaster
classes.tagline: The summoner warlock — an elemental spirit fights beside you while your curses grind everything down.
classes.overview: Spiritmaster fights through a summoned elemental (Fire Spirit is the representative damage spirit) layered with damage-over-time curses. Raw-damage lists rank it S-tier (game8) while group-utility lists hold it at B — the truth is pet-management-dependent.
classes.playstyle: Keep the spirit commanded onto the right target, stack DoTs across enemies, and reposition freely while damage continues. Pet aggro discipline is the class's real skill check.
strengths: S-tier raw damage rating (game8)
A-tier Abyss PvP rating (Mobalytics)
Damage continues while you reposition or kite
Spirit bodyblocks and tanks trash effectively
weaknesses: B-tier on group-utility PvE lists
Pet management adds real complexity
DoT ramp wastes time on trash that dies instantly

skillChains.name: Spirit Command
skillChains.description: The pet-control loop — summon, stance, and command cycles that keep the spirit doing real damage.
steps: Ensure the spirit is summoned before the pull (the cast is long)
Set the aggression stance for damage phases
Command the spirit onto the priority target
Swap to a tanking stance when adds need holding
tips: Watch the spirit's aggro, not just your own bars — it's your second health bar
Re-summon between encounters, never mid-fight

skillChains.name: Curse Cascade
skillChains.description: The DoT stacker — layered curses that tick through whole phases while you handle mechanics.
steps: Apply your damage-over-time curses to the priority target
Spread curses across packs during add phases
Refresh at roughly half duration — fallen DoTs cost more cast time to restore
Keep casting while running; DoTs don't need you to stand still
tips: Fire Spirit is the representative burst pet — command it during burn windows
The Shugo Festival and Sealed Dungeons feed the skill boards that power this rotation

macros.name: Pet Command
macros.useCase: Sends the spirit onto your target and starts the DoT stack in one held press. Delay 10–20 ms low ping / 40–50 ms high ping.

macros.name: Attrition Stack
macros.useCase: Applies the core curse pair without thinking about it — bottom slot highest priority.

priority: Craft the gold Chalice first and lock your core curse/attack skill
Weapon Damage Amplification > Crit/General Amp > Max Attack
Spirit scaling follows your stats — amplification empowers the pet too
Only enhance gold cards with 3–4 Spiritmaster skill lines
arcana.notes: Cards from Transcendence dungeons (entry: Lv 45 + 2,200 GS) are the main source — Mysterious Crystals from Awakening Battle milestones fund the guaranteed-skill transmutations.

priority: Clear the 4 skill boards first (+4 total skill levels — pet and curse nodes)
Attack nodes next; skip MP/crit-resist nodes
PvE: Ariel board; PvP: Azphel board
Skip known PvP-useless nodes (Multi-hit Resist, Crit Damage Tolerance)
daevanion.notes: Skill boards (Nezekan ~13, Zikel 20, Vaizel 30, Triniel 40) contain every active and passive skill once — fully clearing adds +4 skill levels across the kit.

gearProgression.notes: The spirit carries early content — gear matters less here than any other class.
Single weapon slot keeps transfer costs low — invest early.
DoT pressure shines in the long encounters of this tier.
Accept the support-damage role in raids — your DoTs carry the phases between burn windows.

classes.name: Cleric
classes.tagline: The only dedicated healer in AION 2 — the reason your raid attempt survives attempt #4.
classes.overview: Cleric is the game's sole main healer and the second pillar of the group meta (S-tier on both BlueStacks and Mobalytics PvE lists). Every serious group builds around one — Conquest can be rerolled, a dead healer cannot.
classes.playstyle: Track party health bars, pre-cast big heals during scripted damage, and manage mana like a resource bar you're raid-leading with. In PvP Clerics heal from the backline and peel with CC — S-tier on Mobalytics' Abyss list.
strengths: Only dedicated healer at launch — permanent raid demand
S-tier PvE (group-utility lists) and S-tier PvP (Mobalytics)
Heals, cleanses and resurrections in one kit
Medium difficulty with instant group queues
weaknesses: Minimal solo damage output
Mana pressure in long fights
A recent heal nerf (Oct 2026 balance pass) tightened the margin for error

skillChains.name: Radiant Recovery
skillChains.description: The core healing loop — pre-casts, renewals and big heals timed against the boss's damage script.
steps: Pre-cast your big heal before scripted damage, not after
Keep your renewal-type heal ticking on the tank at all times
Top off between patterns with efficient heals
Cleanse debuffs the moment they land — most tick harder than the boss
tips: Learn each boss's damage script — pre-casting is the true gear upgrade
Sanctuary raids allow 2 revives — save resurrections for safe windows

skillChains.name: Punish & Peel
skillChains.description: The Cleric's damage and control suite — Condemnation and interrupts for quiet phases.
steps: Cast Condemnation during no-damage phases to contribute damage
Interrupt or CC divers that reach the backline
Weave mana recovery between damage windows
Re-anchor behind the raid before the next scripted hit
tips: Mana wasted is healing wasted — manage it actively in raids
Your CC is a raid tool: coordinate it with the Templar's interrupts

macros.name: Tank Saver
macros.useCase: Shield-then-heal emergency combo on one held key. Delay 10–20 ms low ping / 40–50 ms high ping, Skill Queue OFF.

macros.name: Cleanup Loop
macros.useCase: Removes debuffs and patches the target in a single press — the loop you'll press most in raids.

priority: Craft the gold Chalice first and lock your core heal skill
Healing amplification over damage stats — every point multiplies your entire kit
Magic Armor (defensive) set pieces fit the Cleric's risk profile
Only enhance gold cards with 3–4 Cleric skill lines
arcana.notes: Arcana card slots (Chalice, Parchment, Bell, Mirror, Scales, Key, Hourglass, Dice, Lantern) take mixable 2/4-piece set bonuses — defensive sets are a legitimate Cleric endgame.

priority: Clear the 4 skill boards first (+4 total skill levels — heal nodes first)
Then survivability nodes — dead Clerics heal nothing
Attack nodes last; skip MP/crit-resist nodes
PvE: Ariel board; PvP: Azphel board (Cleric is S-tier in the Abyss — invest there)
daevanion.notes: Node costs: gray 1, green 2, blue 3, orange 4. The Oct 2026 heal nerf makes the skill-level nodes even more valuable — +4 skill levels is a real throughput bump.

gearProgression.notes: Quest gear heals fine — save materials for the keeper tier.
Healers get the most value out of early transfer investment.
Mana-efficiency rolls matter as much as raw healing here.
Bracelets are raid-only progression — your weekly Ludra kills fund them.

classes.name: Chanter
classes.tagline: The hybrid battle-support — buff mantras, Dark Crush combos and off-heals in one staff package.
classes.overview: Chanter is the group-utility darling: S-tier on Mobalytics PvE and PvP lists and S-tier on BlueStacks. Spinning Strike and Impactful Crush open Dark Crush, and its buff mantras amplify the whole party while it off-heals and melees.
classes.playstyle: Keep buff mantras live (their downtime is party damage downtime), run the Spinning Strike → Impactful Crush → Dark Crush combo in melee, and weave off-heals between windows. In PvP Chanters buff the push and strip priority targets — S-tier in the Abyss.
strengths: S-tier PvE and PvP on group-utility lists
Party-wide mantras amplify every damage dealer
Dark Crush combo adds real melee damage
Off-heals cover light damage phases
weaknesses: Not as strong as Cleric at raw healing
Not as strong as Gladiator at raw damage
A recent PvP nerf (Oct 2026) trimmed its Abyss dominance

skillChains.name: Dark Crush Setup
skillChains.description: The documented Chanter combo — Spinning Strike and Impactful Crush conditionally unlock Dark Crush, your heavy melee hit.
steps: Open with Spinning Strike
Chain Impactful Crush to unlock Dark Crush
Fire Dark Crush the moment it lights up
Reset the loop with your basic attack skill
tips: Stack the combo into one Skill Macro slot (bottom = highest priority) and hold the key
Melee uptime matters — you're a support who hits, not a DPS who occasionally buffs

skillChains.name: Mantra Cycle
skillChains.description: The buff engine — maintaining the mantra set the entire party scales from.
steps: Open with your attack mantra before the pull
Layer the defense mantra as the fight settles
Refresh both before they fall off — never let them lapse
Swap in the recovery mantra during heavy damage phases
tips: Check mantra timers every rotation — lapses are invisible in logs but huge in damage
Only a limited mantra set runs at once: pick per fight, not per mood

macros.name: Dark Crush Combo
macros.useCase: Documented unlock combo as one official Skill Macro slot — hold the key to cycle, delay 10–20 ms low ping / 40–50 ms high ping, Skill Queue OFF.

macros.name: Mantra Refresh
macros.useCase: Keeps both party mantras alive on one button — press it on cooldown during fights.

priority: Craft the gold Chalice first and lock Dark Crush
Buff/utility amplification over personal damage stats
Weapon Damage Amplification > Crit/General Amp > Max Attack for the melee half
Only enhance gold cards with 3–4 Chanter skill lines
arcana.notes: Chanter multiplies the party, so Arcana lines that empower mantras and Dark Crush outvalue raw attack — the 2/4-piece set bonuses do a lot of quiet work.

priority: Clear the 4 skill boards first (+4 total skill levels — Dark Crush and mantra nodes)
Then attack nodes (you're in melee), then utility
Skip MP/crit-resist nodes and the known PvP-useless nodes
PvE: Ariel board; PvP: Azphel board
daevanion.notes: Boards unlock at ~13/20/30/40 (Nezekan, Zikel, Vaizel, Triniel). The Oct 2026 Chanter PvP nerf makes the Azphel board's percent-stat nodes the comeback path.

gearProgression.notes: Mantra uptime practice > gear while leveling.
Staff first, mantra-relevant armor second.
Melee uptime at this tier decides your real contribution.
Your logs show buff uptime and interrupts — the gear just stops you dying.
